cerita:
Seorang pensyarah pernah bertanya kepada semua pelajar dalam kelas: kenapa sambung pengajian Sarjana? Jawapan saya mudah. Sejak hari pertama, saya sambung belajar kerana anak saya.

Ali autistik dan ADHD, dan tidak semua tempat mampu menerima dia. Apa yang saya belajar tentang perkembangan kanak-kanak, psikologi, pembelajaran dan tingkah laku, saya cuba terapkan di rumah. Saya juga bersedia dengan pelan B, termasuk homeschooling, jika suatu hari nanti diperlukan.

Ali adalah sebab saya bermula. Semoga ilmu yang saya kumpul nanti bukan sahaja membantu Ali, tetapi juga ibu bapa lain yang melalui perjalanan yang sama.
tajuk_en: Why I went back for my Master's
cerita_en:
A lecturer once asked everyone in class why they chose to do a Master's degree. My answer was simple: from day one, I did it because of my son.

Ali is autistic and has ADHD, and not every place has been able to accept him. Everything I learn about child development, psychology, learning and behaviour, I try to apply at home. I also need a plan B, including homeschooling, in case he ever needs it.

Ali is the reason I started. I hope that what I learn along the way will help not only him, but other parents on the same journey.

tajuk: Melihat anak autistik melangkaui cabaran mereka
cerita:
Bila saya memilih media sosial untuk menyebarkan kesedaran tentang anak-anak berkeperluan khas, saya juga memilih untuk menjaga maruah dan privasi anak. Sebab itu, apa yang orang nampak tentang Ali kebanyakannya adalah kekuatan, pencapaian dan sisi indah menjadi autistik.

Bukan bermakna Ali tidak pernah meltdown. Realiti itu penting untuk dikongsi. Tetapi jika anak hanya dipaparkan ketika paling rapuh, kita perlu fikir kesannya terhadap maruah mereka dan cara masyarakat melihat mereka.

Dulu, soalan pertama orang selalu "Dia tantrum tak?". Hari ini semakin ramai ibu bapa berkongsi kebolehan anak-anak autistik. Dan jika seorang anak tiada kelebihan luar biasa sekalipun, mereka tetap berharga dan layak dihormati.
tajuk_en: Seeing autistic children beyond their struggles
cerita_en:
When I chose social media to raise awareness about children with special needs, I also chose to protect my child's dignity and privacy. That is why most of what people see about Ali shows his strengths, his achievements and the beautiful sides of being autistic.

It doesn't mean Ali never has meltdowns. Showing reality matters. But if children are only ever shown at their most vulnerable, we need to think about what that does to their dignity and to how society sees them.

People used to ask first, "Does he have tantrums?" Today more parents share what their autistic children can do. And even a child without any extraordinary ability is still precious and deserves respect.

tajuk: "I'm autistic, and I have super abilities"
cerita:
Sekarang, setiap kali Ali berjumpa orang baharu, beginilah dia memperkenalkan diri: "Hi, my name is Ameer Ali. My mummy says I'm a superhero. I'm autistic, and I have super abilities."

Dia tahu siapa dirinya, dan dia bangga. Saya mahu Ali membesar dengan satu keyakinan: autisme adalah sebahagian daripada dirinya, tetapi tidak menentukan segala yang dia boleh capai.
tajuk_en: "I'm autistic, and I have super abilities"
cerita_en:
These days, whenever Ali meets someone new, this is how he introduces himself: "Hi, my name is Ameer Ali. My mummy says I'm a superhero. I'm autistic, and I have super abilities."

He knows who he is, and he is proud of it. I want Ali to grow up knowing that autism is part of who he is, but it doesn't define everything he can be.

cerita:
Hari ini saya bawa Ali ke Hari Kokurikulum SK Taman Ria, sekolah lama saya. Alhamdulillah, Ali turut menang cabutan bertuah.

Satu perkembangan yang saya perasan: Ali semakin boleh menyesuaikan diri dengan suasana bising dan tempat yang ramai orang. Langkah kecil seperti ini sangat bermakna bagi kami.
tajuk_en: Co-curricular Day at SK Taman Ria
cerita_en:
Today I took Ali to the Co-curricular Day at SK Taman Ria, my old primary school. He even won a lucky draw prize.

One change I noticed: Ali is coping better and better with noise and crowded places. Small steps like this mean a lot to us.

tajuk: Saya bukan pakar, saya seorang ibu
cerita:
Sejak saya berkongsi tentang autisme, banyak mesej masuk melalui Threads, TikTok dan e-mel bertanyakan pendapat dan cara mendapatkan diagnosis. Saya hargai setiap satu.

Cuma saya ingin jelaskan, saya bukan OT, ahli terapi pertuturan atau doktor. Saya seorang ibu yang berkongsi pengalaman membesarkan anak autistik, sambil menjalankan kajian tentang penglibatan ibu bapa dalam kalangan keluarga yang mempunyai anak autistik.

Saya percaya, parents need parents. Kita perlukan circle yang memahami, bukan menghakimi.
tajuk_en: I'm not an expert, I'm a mother
cerita_en:
Since I started sharing about autism, many messages have come in through Threads, TikTok and email asking for advice and how to get a diagnosis. I appreciate every one of them.

I do want to be clear: I'm not an OT, a speech therapist or a doctor. I'm a mother sharing my experience of raising an autistic child, while researching parental involvement among families of autistic children.

I believe parents need parents. We need a circle that understands, not one that judges.

tajuk: Kajian: ibu bapa kanak-kanak autisme di PPKI
cerita:
Saya sedang menjalankan kajian akademik sebagai sebahagian daripada program Sarjana Pendidikan di Universiti Utara Malaysia (UUM). Kajian ini memberi fokus kepada perkongsian sekolah dan keluarga, sokongan komuniti serta penglibatan ibu bapa dalam menyokong kanak-kanak autisme di Program Pendidikan Khas Integrasi (PPKI).

Jika anda ibu bapa atau penjaga kanak-kanak autisme yang belajar di PPKI, pandangan anda sangat bermakna. Soal selidik mengambil masa 6 hingga 8 minit dan tanpa nama: https://forms.gle/2DPb6b9yFr7uUrXs6
tajuk_en: Survey: parents of autistic children in PPKI
cerita_en:
I'm carrying out an academic study as part of my Master of Education at Universiti Utara Malaysia (UUM). It looks at school–family partnership, community support and parental involvement in supporting autistic children in Malaysia's Integrated Special Education Programme (PPKI).

If you are the parent or carer of an autistic child in PPKI, your views matter a great deal. The anonymous survey takes 6 to 8 minutes: https://forms.gle/2DPb6b9yFr7uUrXs6

tajuk: Terapi percuma di hospital dan sekolah pendidikan khas
cerita:
Ramai bertanya di mana Ali menjalani terapi carakerja (OT). Dari umur 3 hingga 5 tahun, Ali ke pusat terapi swasta. Sejak bersekolah, Ali hanya ke terapi kerajaan: OT di Hospital Tuanku Fauziah dan 3PK di Sekolah Pendidikan Khas Perlis. Kedua-duanya percuma.

Setiap sesi, saya lebih banyak mendengar dan berbincang: apa yang Ali masih lemah, apa yang boleh dibuat di rumah, dan perkembangan yang semakin baik. Bagi saya, terapi bukan hanya di dalam bilik terapi. Apa yang kita teruskan di rumah sama penting.
tajuk_en: Free therapy at the hospital and special education school
cerita_en:
Many people ask where Ali goes for occupational therapy (OT). From age 3 to 5 he attended a private centre. Since starting school he only goes to government therapy: OT at Hospital Tuanku Fauziah and 3PK at Sekolah Pendidikan Khas Perlis. Both are free.

At each session I mostly listen and discuss: where Ali still struggles, what we can do at home, and where he is improving. For me, therapy doesn't only happen in the therapy room. What we continue at home matters just as much.

cerita:
ADHD bukan sekadar tidak boleh duduk diam. Ada jenis yang lebih banyak berlaku dalam minda (Inattentive: mudah terganggu, mudah lupa, susah mengurus), dan ada yang lebih ketara pada tingkah laku (Hyperactive-Impulsive: susah duduk diam, susah menunggu giliran, bertindak secara impulsif). Di rumah kami, kedua-duanya ada.

Antara yang saya amalkan: rutin harian yang konsisten, arahan yang jelas dan ringkas, pecahkan tugasan besar kepada langkah kecil, puji tingkah laku positif, fahami tingkah laku sebagai komunikasi, dan kawal emosi sendiri. Bila kita faham bagaimana ADHD berfungsi, banyak perkara menjadi lebih lancar.
cerita_en:
ADHD isn't only about not sitting still. One type happens mostly on the inside (Inattentive: easily distracted, forgetful, struggling to organise), and another shows more in behaviour (Hyperactive-Impulsive: restless, finding it hard to wait, acting on impulse). Our home has both.

What I try to practise: a consistent daily routine, short and clear instructions, breaking big tasks into small steps, praising positive behaviour, seeing behaviour as communication, and staying calm myself. Once we understand how ADHD works, many things go more smoothly.

tajuk: Artikel pertama saya di NeuroNestHub, Singapura
cerita:
Alhamdulillah, artikel pertama saya tentang perjalanan membesarkan anak AuDHD, "My Journey as a Mother of an AuDHD Child", telah diterbitkan di NeuroNestHub, Singapura. Pengasas NeuroNestHub sendiri menjemput saya menulis untuk platform mereka.

Saya percaya pengalaman juga satu bentuk ilmu, yang lahir daripada kesabaran, pembacaan, terapi dan kasih sayang. Semoga ia memberi harapan kepada ibu bapa lain, dan menjadi langkah pertama ke arah PhD dalam bidang ini.

Baca artikel: https://neuronesthub.com/my-journey-as-a-mother-of-an-audhd-child/
tajuk_en: My first article on NeuroNestHub, Singapore
cerita_en:
My first article about raising an AuDHD child, "My Journey as a Mother of an AuDHD Child", has been published on NeuroNestHub in Singapore. The founder of NeuroNestHub invited me to write for the platform.

I believe experience is also a form of knowledge, born of patience, reading, therapy and love. I hope it gives other parents hope, and that it is a first step towards a PhD in this field.

Read the article: https://neuronesthub.com/my-journey-as-a-mother-of-an-audhd-child/
